label: clean-recipient qualification harness

rows.claim: The distribution package exists and is identified
The package carries a Developer ID Installer signature, so Gatekeeper can accept it
rows.detail: the package is unsigned (ad-hoc local build); a recipient's Gatekeeper will refuse it, so the just-works claim cannot be made for these bytes

rows.claim: The installer declares a minimum OS and remains arm64-only
Every executable in the payload is arm64 and needs no newer OS than declared
Approved payload code declares macOS 14.0; the pinned engine keeps its upstream floor
The shipped removal utility is bounded and refuses unrecognized paths
Gatekeeper assessment is enabled and was not weakened for this test
A quarantined copy carries the download attribute
Gatekeeper's assessment of the quarantined installer, with normal protections in place

detail.note: This is the measurement a recipient would get. It is not worked around: no xattr removal, no spctl override, no right-click recipe.

rows.claim: The recipient's Git situation, reported rather than assumed

detail.note: This host has Command Line Tools, so it cannot stand in for a clean recipient. Packaged Mona refuses Apple's CLT stub rather than triggering the installer, so Git features report unavailable on a machine without Git.

rows.claim: The host this matrix ran on

detail.note: A development host with Xcode CLT, Homebrew and a cached engine. It cannot prove the absence of those things.

rows.claim: A separate Apple silicon Mac or clean supported VM runs the exact signed installer through quarantine
rows.detail: requires a second host or VM; this repository has neither

rows.claim: The standard Installer authentication prompt completes without a terminal step
rows.detail: requires an administrator prompt on the recipient host

rows.claim: The installed app launches from Applications and the Finder Service opens a folder
rows.detail: requires the install above; the LaunchServices launch itself is proven for the local build (R13)

rows.claim: A secure provider setup on a machine with no cached credential
rows.detail: requires a user account that has never run Codewhale; this builds on second-user evidence, which the prompt says is not proof

rows.claim: Offline local operation before any provider is configured
rows.detail: requires a recipient with no network path to a provider and no cached engine config

rows.claim: A denied or revoked folder permission produces a clear, non-destructive refusal
rows.detail: requires manipulating TCC, which needs interactive consent

rows.claim: A locked keychain is reported, not retried into a loop
rows.detail: requires a locked login keychain on the recipient

rows.claim: Sleep and wake leave the runtime in a stated state
rows.detail: requires a physical lid close or a real suspend; simulated suspend is already covered by the lifecycle smoke

rows.claim: Two users on one Mac do not share state or credentials
rows.detail: requires a second account with administrator authorization

rows.claim: An unsupported macOS version is refused by the installer rather than half-installed
rows.detail: requires a host below 14.0; the requirement is declared and the enforcement is in the preinstall script

rows.claim: A clean reinstall, an upgrade over the previous build and an uninstall all behave
rows.detail: the rehearsals and the P23 lifecycle smoke cover the mechanisms under isolated roots; the recipient run is the part that needs the host

reasons: artifact.signed: the package is unsigned (ad-hoc local build); a recipient's Gatekeeper will refuse it, so the just-works claim cannot be made for these bytes
